root_cause: In parent BuiltinsTypedArrayStubBuilder::Filter, the copy loop writes to newArray while passing arrayType captured from thisValue. The callback runs before allocation, so it can install a constructor on the receiver; HasConstructor reads the receiver HClass bit and NewTypedArray then routes through TypedArraySpeciesCreate. That helper accepts a constructed TypedArray if its length is at least requested and its ContentType matches the exemplar; it does not require the same element type. For example, an Int32Array receiver can use a species constructor returning a Uint8Array of the requested length. The parent then passes Int32 jsType into the store. FastSetPropertyByIndex checks index against the destination length but computes byte offset and write type from jsType; the inspected FastSetValueInBuffer path performs detached check and writes by computed type/byteIndex without a destination byte-length argument. For n=3, the final index 2 with four-byte Int32 width computes offset 8 and a four-byte write against a three-byte Uint8 backing store. The on-heap ByteArray allocation rounds its data extent from three to eight bytes; the write ends four bytes beyond the aligned ByteArray object allocation, so this concrete source-level scenario does not depend on integer overflow or allocator padding assumptions. The fixed source obtains the actual destination HClass type before storing. This is a concrete static out-of-bounds write candidate under the described callback/species path, supported by the source. Runtime reproduction, full-build path equivalence, allocator effects, product applicability and security impact remain unverified.

evidence.claim: Filter allocates newArray after the callback/filter loop, checks allocation exception state, then copies kept values into that destination.
The parent copy loop stores into newArray while passing arrayType captured from thisValue to StoreTypedArrayElement.
The fixed source loads newArrayType from the allocated destination and passes it to StoreTypedArrayElement.
The store helper passes jsType to SetTypeArrayPropertyByIndex after detached-buffer and index-range checks.
Filter dispatches the callback before allocating the output TypedArray. The callback path can execute user JavaScript before the subsequent NewTypedArray call observes constructor/prototype state.
NewTypedArray can take a TypedArraySpeciesCreate slow path when constructor, species marker, or object marker checks fail; its implementation is unchanged between parent and fixed commits.
Runtime stub converts passed jsType and dispatches it to JSTypedArray::FastSetPropertyByIndex.
FastSetPropertyByIndex checks index against the destination array length but computes byte offset and element type from passed jsType.

FastSetValueInBuffer checks detached state then obtains the data pointer and delegates to SetValueInBuffer; the inspected SetValueInBuffer switch writes by type at byteIndex and does not take a buffer length. This local call path alone does not prove there are no checks elsewhere.

If destination element width is less than passed source jsType width, the computed byte offset for later indices may extend past destination backing storage; an out-of-bounds write is therefore a candidate requiring dynamic validation.
The fast Filter calls user callback before constructing newArray; after callback it calls NewTypedArray with captured source arrayType and then uses that same arrayType in every parent output store.
HasConstructor reads the HClass HasConstructor bit, enabling callback-created constructor property to send the later NewTypedArray call to slow species path.
TypedArraySpeciesCreate slow path constructs the selected species, requires a TypedArray, length at least requested and matching ContentType, but does not require matching element type.

Concrete static scenario: an Int32Array species result of Uint8Array length n>=2 is permitted by the same ContentType and minimum-length checks; parent uses four-byte Int32 offsets for indices 0..n-1, so the final four-byte write ends at offset 4n against n-byte storage.
Adding a constructor property to a TypedArray transitions to an HClass with HasConstructor set, so the user callback can cause the later NewTypedArray check to take its species slow path.

If the Uint8Array species result is longer than n, the particular final-write overrun depends on its backing byte length; the stated exact-length n case is accepted by the length lower-bound check and provides the narrow static candidate. Results with sufficient extra length can avoid this specific bound crossing.

On-heap TypedArray allocation computes byteLength as destination elementSize times length, calls NewByteArray(arrayLength, elementSize) below the on-heap threshold, and records exact byteLength and arrayLength on the destination. A Uint8Array(n) species result therefore has n logical backing bytes.

ByteArray computes raw object size as DATA_OFFSET + elementSize*length, GetData points to DATA_OFFSET + index*elementSize, and object alignment is 8 bytes. For a 3-byte Uint8 backing area, object allocation padding is five bytes; the candidate final write range [8,12) relative to data extends four bytes past the aligned ByteArray object extent.

NewByteArray aligns DATA_OFFSET + elementSize*length to object alignment before allocating, so the n=3 Int32-to-Uint8 candidate final write [8,12) relative to data exceeds the aligned object allocation by four bytes.

protections.condition: Detached-buffer and index-range guards prevent writes for detached buffers and out-of-range indices; they do not validate jsType against the destination type.

Filter checks fast typed array, detached input, constructor/prototype/accessor guards before the callback loop; these checks do not directly establish that the allocated destination type equals the captured source arrayType.

entry_attacker_trigger_impact.trigger: Static scenario: during Int32Array Filter callback, install a constructor/species that returns Uint8Array(3). Species construction accepts it because it is a TypedArray with matching Number ContentType and length equal to requested result count. Parent copy index 2 uses Int32 jsType: byte offset 8, four-byte write [8,12); the Uint8 backing data is 3 bytes and its ByteArray allocation is 8-byte aligned, so source layout arithmetic extends the write four bytes beyond the allocated object. Runtime build path/reproduction remains unverified.
